text:
maria zhang: Heads-up: CustX returned their security questionnaire. Major asks: proof-of-rotation (signed), option for customer-held key material, SIEM-ready audit exports, and IR timelines for Private deployments. Need a short draft we can send.

jamal singh: quick clarifying q: when they say "proof-of-rotation" do they expect key escrow or a signed attestation that the rotation happened?

maria zhang: they want both options laid out. preferred is customer-kept keys (BYOK) but they want an auditable artifact from our side proving we served using rotated keys and who initiated it.

alex harris: we can issue a rotation manifest that is append-only and signed by our rotation service using an org-level rotation key. Manifest includes old_key_id, new_key_id, rotated_by, timestamp, and a manifest signature (sha256). Recommend a per-tenant rotation service account so the principal is obvious.

natalie chen: +1 on per-tenant service account. That keeps operator identities separate from automation. @jamal can you confirm current behavior for Dedicated vs Private?

jamal singh: Dedicated: we already create tenant-scoped service principals. Private: if customer opts for customer-managed KMS (BYOK) we do not create keys in their HSM; we can still emit our signed manifest but hsm-signed attestations require the customer's HSM provider to run their attestation flow. For Redwood-managed KMS in Private, we create tenant principals.

rohit patel: two customer-facing caveats to include: (1) HSM attestation vs manifest: we can provide our signed manifest always; HSM quotes/attestations are gated by the HSM vendor and often require an on-demand audit or customer permission. (2) SIEM export formats: we can stream JSONL to S3, HTTP(S) webhook, Syslog, or Splunk forwarder; we need endpoint details and retention policy in the SOW.

alex harris: propose an example manifest we can paste in the questionnaire:```json
{
  "tenant_id": "custx-45",
  "event": "kms_key_rotation",
  "old_key": "key-7a3f",
  "new_key": "key-09f3",
  "rotated_by": "sa:kms-rotator:custx-45",
  "time": "2026-02-14T22:15:03Z",
  "manifest_sig": "sha256:fb12e9...",
  "hsm_attestation": "available-on-request"
}
```

natalie chen: add an IR SLA paragraph: Acknowledge within 15m, initial triage within 1h, containment plan within 4h, and forensic artifact collection started within 24h (for Private deployments). Note: coordination with customer for on-prem HSM evidence may extend timelines.

maria zhang: can someone draft a short checkbox-style response for their tracker? Should be bite-sized for auditors.

jamal singh: I'll draft the checklist. Items: 1) BYOK support (yes/no + instructions), 2) Per-tenant rotation service account (yes), 3) Signed rotation manifests retained for 1 year (default), 4) Audit log retention (90d default, configurable), 5) SIEM export destinations (S3/Splunk/Syslog/webhook), 6) IR SLAs and contact sync, 7) HSM attestation note (vendor-dependent).

rohit patel: vuln triage note to include: if rotation is performed because of suspected compromise, we will rotate dependent secrets (model keys, API tokens) and invalidate any KV caches referencing the compromised key. That should be in the runbook and caller checklist.

alex harris: adding a short log sample auditors like to see:```text
Feb 14 22:15:03 redwood-kms[rotator]: tenant=custx-45 event=kms_key_rotation old_key=key-7a3f new_key=key-09f3 rotated_by=sa:kms-rotator:custx-45 manifest_sig=sha256:fb12e9...
Feb 14 22:15:04 redwood-audit: tenant=custx-45 event=grant subject=sa:ingest:type=syslog request_id=req-zz-998
```

maria zhang: Deploy-bot, can you point to the current IR runbook we should reference?

deploy-bot: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ir-private-deployments|IR runbook (private)> :paperclip: 

natalie chen: after Jamal posts the checklist and a one-paragraph RBAC blurb, I'll assemble the questionnaire response and loop in Legal for the HSM wording.

maria zhang: action items: Jamal = checklist + RBAC blurb by EOD, Alex = manifest + log samples (done), Rohit = estimate connector work for Splunk push if they want on-prem ingestion.

jamal singh: will post the checklist and short RBAC blurb by 18:00 PT. Flag: if they want a managed Splunk connector we need 2-3 sprint lead time (small infra + security review).

rohit patel: noted. I'll ask CustX for their Splunk endpoint, cert thumbprint, and retention reqs before scoping.

maria zhang: thanks all. Once Jamal's checklist is in I'll send the draft to CustX security and schedule a 30m review call if they want to walk through the artifacts. :thumbsup:
